newsitem.title: USA: Walden sees lower-than-expected Q2 FFO.
newsitem.headline: Walden sees lower-than-expected Q2 FFO.

text.p: Walden Residential Properties Inc said Monday it expected its second quarter funds from operations to be lower than it earlier anticipated.

The company said it expected its second-quarter funds from operations to range between $0.48 to $0.50 a share, including a one-time charge of $0.01 a share, compared with $0.52 a share in the same period the year before.

It attributed the decline to a delay in the acquisition of seven properties from Drever Partners and a drop in the average occupancy rate of Walden's properties to 94 percent from 95 percent the year before.
The real estate investment trust said it was taking a charge of $200,000, or $0.01 a share, in the second quarter related to management changes.
Walden said on May 9 it agreed to buy private Drever for $670 million, $380 million in stock, warrants and cash, and $290 million in assumed debt. It expected to close the deal by October.

The trust said Monday its second-quarter funds from operations would have been $0.02 higher had the acquisition of seven (out of 79) Drever properties been closed as originally scheduled in March 1997.

It also said the lower occupancy rate of its properties will result in a lower-than-expected 1.5 percent increase in "same-store" revenue, which will reduce projected second-quarter funds from operations by about $0.04 a share.
Chief executive Don Daseke said in a statement he expected Drever's properties to be accretive to the trust's fund from operations by about $0.10 a share in 1998.

He also said the company is restructuring its management. When the Drever deal closes, all Walden property operations will report to Mike Collier, who has managed the Drever portfolio for 10 years, he said, adding Walden's executive vice president of operations, Steve Lamberti, is leaving to pursue other interests.
Walden owns and manages 75 properties with 23,188 apartment units, the company said. Its stock closed at 25-7/8 Monday, up 5/16.
